entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Faustus of Mileve was a prominent Manichaean bishop of the 4th century, hailing from the Numidian city of Milevis. He rose from a poor, pagan background to become a highly respected teacher, preacher, and debater.




Faustus' significance in the annals of Manichaean history cannot be overstated, particularly in his encounter with the future St. Augustine of Hippo in Carthage around 383 CE. This pivotal event marked a turning point in the development of Manichaeism in the Western world.




Despite his relatively short life, Faustus left a lasting legacy in the world of early Christian theology, with his debates and teachings influencing the thoughts of Augustine and other prominent Christian thinkers.




As a testament to his enduring impact, the records of Faustus' life and teachings continue to be studied by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complex religious and cultural landscape of the 4th century Mediterranean.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Faustus of Mileve was a significant figure in the development of Manichaeism in the Western world, particularly in his encounter with Augustine of Hippo in Carthage around 383 CE. This event had a lasting impact on the shaping of Christian theology in the region.
